doc.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Young black musicians in traditional jazz
summary: Gordon says some young black musicians in New Orleans, such as Wallace Davenport, Wendell Brunious and the Marsalis family, are returning to this music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Do you, when we look at the players that are playing this kind of music today, it seems to be rare to see a black musician, a young black musician playing this kind of music. Do you have any thoughts on that?

Well there is, if you go down to New Orleans now there’s a few of them that are coming back and playing this type of music. Wallace Davenport and Wendell Brunious, and a few others, Wynton Marsallis and his brother are playing or taking up, the young blacks are coming back again with jazz more in the forefront.
Well that was actually a great answer. I’m glad I asked the question. It sounds like you know your history. Was clarinet your first instrument?
